nodes.norm_label: unpack the advertised temperature and humidity, if present. int16 temperature...

nodes.label: CFG_TX_POWER Override (0x18 -> 0x1F)
nodes.rationale: At the CubeMX default 0x18 (-0.15 dBm) the board reads ~-86 dBm at 30 cm on this host's adapter, below the level at which a 15-30 s scan reliably catches a 1 s advertising interval, so it was never seen. At 0x1F (+6 dBm, stack maximum) it reads -80..-82 dBm, ~3 reports per 45 s scan, and connects. Overridden from the USER CODE BEGIN PD block in app_ble.c because the define sits outside any CubeMX user section, the same pattern already used for the advertising interval.

nodes.label: Weak RF Path (still open)
nodes.rationale: -80 dBm at 30 cm with +6 dBm transmit power is roughly 50 dB worse than expected for this module; antenna, matching network or host adapter placement is the next suspect if the link must be better than 'works on the desk'.

nodes.label: APPD_Init() Never Called
nodes.rationale: The APPE_Init_1 user block in app_entry.c was empty, so DbgTraceInit() never ran and every APP_DBG_MSG went nowhere even with CFG_DEBUG_*_TRACE set to 1. This is why nothing about the weak RF link could be observed.

nodes.label: DbgOutputInit() Link Error on MX_USART1_UART_Init
nodes.rationale: app_debug.c called MX_USART1_UART_Init(), which is static in main.c, causing a link error. Removed because main() already brings USART1 up before MX_APPE_Init().

nodes.label: CLK48 HSEM Lock Before Stack Start
nodes.rationale: LL_HSEM_1StepLock(HSEM, 5) is taken in main.c before the stack starts, as 004_sen55_ble_app does. A latent bug, A/B tested as NOT the cause of the advertising silence; fixed on its own merits.
nodes.norm_label: clk48 hsem lock before stack start

nodes.label: PA9 Does Not Reach ST-Link V3 VCP
nodes.rationale: /dev/ttyACM0 (the V3 VCP) stayed silent while the MCU was provably transmitting (USART1 ISR = 0x6000D0 with TC and TXE set, PA9/PA10 in AF7, BRR 0x226 = 115107 baud). A Waveshare CH340 adapter on /dev/ttyACM1 on the same PA9 pin printed everything immediately, so the bench wiring, not the MCU, is at fault.
nodes.norm_label: pa9 does not reach st-link v3 vcp

nodes.label: Trace and STOP2 Are Mutually Exclusive
nodes.rationale: CFG_DEBUG_TRACE != 0 force-clears CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED, so debug trace and Phase 6's STOP2 can never be enabled at the same time. Trace must be turned off for power work.
nodes.norm_label: trace and stop2 are mutually exclusive

nodes.label: aci_hal_set_radio_activity_mask Useless on This Coprocessor FW
nodes.rationale: Dead end. On wireless FW 1.22.1 / FUS 2.0.0, even mask 0xFFFF yields zero ACI_HAL_END_OF_RADIO_ACTIVITY events while the board is provably advertising. Absence of those events is not evidence of a dead radio.
nodes.norm_label: aci_hal_set_radio_activity_mask useless on this coprocessor fw

nodes.label: Scan HCI Commands Unsupported (no central/observer role)
nodes.rationale: Dead end. hci_le_set_scan_parameters / hci_le_set_scan_enable return 0x01 (unknown HCI command); this stack build has no central/observer role, so the board cannot scan to test its own RX path.
nodes.norm_label: scan hci commands unsupported (no central/observer role)

nodes.label: Clocks Ruled Out (HSE/LSE verified)
nodes.rationale: RCC->CR HSERDY set, BDCR LSERDY set with RTCSEL=LSE, CSR RFWKPSEL=LSE. Clocks were never the cause.

nodes.label: STM32_Programmer_CLI -coreReg Leaves Core Halted
nodes.rationale: Reading core registers halts the core and leaves it halted; an st-flash reset is required before any on-air test, otherwise the board looks dead.

nodes.label: Advertising Buffer Overflow in app_ble_policy.c
nodes.rationale: The buffer was sized from the value of each AD length byte instead of the field footprint (payload + 2), writing 18 bytes into s_adv_data[17]. Now derived through APP_BLE_AD_FIELD() with a _Static_assert on the 31-byte limit plus a runtime length check. Unrelated to the advertising silence.

nodes.label: Building from Debug/ Requires ST Toolchain
nodes.rationale: CubeIDE subdir.mk files pass -fcyclomatic-complexity, which the Fedora arm-none-eabi-gcc rejects, so ST's bundled GCC must be put on PATH before make all.
nodes.norm_label: building from debug/ requires st toolchain

nodes.label: Battery-Powered Environmental Monitor
nodes.rationale: Priority order is low battery consumption, reliable BLE, fast response to environmental change, then useful display behavior without leaving the OLED powered. Explicitly not optimized for maximum continuous update rate.

nodes.label: Event-Driven Design Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Polling loops with HAL_Delay keep the MCU awake. Every subsystem must let the core sleep in STOP2 and be woken by RTC, BLE event or button, process the event, and return to STOP2.

nodes.label: Adaptive Sampling Strategy
nodes.rationale: The core architectural principle: spend most time asleep and become temporarily more responsive when the environment changes or the user interacts.

nodes.label: APP_STATE_STABLE
nodes.rationale: 20 s sampling, ~1000 ms advertising, OLED off, STOP2 whenever possible; values configurable rather than scattered as magic numbers.

nodes.label: APP_STATE_ACTIVE
nodes.rationale: Entered on |dT| >= 0.10 C or |dRH| >= 1 %; samples at 1 Hz and returns to STABLE after ~30 s of stability.

nodes.label: APP_STATE_INTERACTIVE
nodes.rationale: Entered on a button press; OLED on with immediate refresh for ~10 s, each interaction resetting the timeout, then back to ACTIVE or STABLE.

nodes.label: environment_has_changed()
nodes.rationale: Uses absolute deltas of temperature and humidity. Pressure is measured and exposed over BLE but deliberately does not trigger ACTIVE unless enabled later.

nodes.label: BME280 Forced-Mode Strategy
nodes.rationale: Forced mode is used instead of continuous normal mode so the sensor returns to sleep after every conversion. The conversion wait must be a scheduled timer or short sleep, never a long HAL_Delay.

nodes.label: bme280_driver Module
nodes.rationale: Owns registers, compensation formulas, forced measurements and raw I2C traffic. Must contain no BLE, OLED or adaptive-sampling policy.

nodes.label: oled_driver Module
nodes.rationale: Owns OLED commands, framebuffer, drawing primitives; not responsible for deciding when the OLED turns on.

nodes.label: app_environment Module
nodes.rationale: Owns sensor scheduling, previous/current measurements, change detection and STABLE/ACTIVE transitions.

nodes.label: app_display Module
nodes.rationale: Owns display timeout, deciding when the OLED is awake, formatting readings and invoking the OLED driver.

nodes.label: app_ble_policy Module
nodes.rationale: Owns notification thresholds, connection parameter policy, advertisement payload updates and when new values should be published.

nodes.label: app_power Module
nodes.rationale: Owns the decision to sleep, low-power entry/exit hooks and wake-source handling.

nodes.label: app_config.h Central Configuration
nodes.rationale: All tunable thresholds and intervals live in one header so they are not scattered as unexplained numeric constants across application logic.

nodes.label: AppEvent Bit-Flag Event Model
nodes.rationale: Prefer STM32CubeWB's existing sequencer/scheduling mechanisms; FreeRTOS must not be introduced merely for this feature.

nodes.label: Button Interrupt Handling
nodes.rationale: Interrupt-driven, debounced, ISR limited to recording the event, setting a flag and waking the application. No OLED, BME280 or BLE work in the ISR.

nodes.label: EXTI-Mask Debounce via Timer Server
nodes.rationale: HAL_GetTick() cannot debounce here: stm32_lpm_if.c calls HAL_SuspendTick() on every STOP2 entry, so the tick barely advances while asleep and a tick-difference test swallows presses for seconds to minutes. Instead HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback() masks the EXTI line and re-arms it from an RTC-backed timer-server single shot; button_rearm_cb() clears both EXTI and NVIC pending bits so bounces that arrived while masked are discarded. Window is BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS.

nodes.label: USER_BUTTON on PA15
nodes.rationale: PA15 to GND, GPIO_MODE_IT_FALLING with internal pull-up, EXTI15_10_IRQn at preemption priority 5 — below the timer server's RTC wakeup (3) and above SysTick (15), so it can never preempt the BLE stack's IPCC/HSEM lines at 0. PA15 is JTDI; SWD uses PA13/PA14 so it is free, but the button must not be held while attaching a JTAG (not SWD) probe.

nodes.label: OLED Power Abstraction
nodes.rationale: display_power_on/off/is_powered may initially only send SSD1306 ON/OFF commands and later drive a MOSFET load switch; application logic must not know which implementation is used.

nodes.label: BLE Advertising Policy
nodes.rationale: ~1000 ms configurable interval; latest temperature and humidity carried in advertising data so a scanner can read the room without connecting. Advertising frequency must never be raised just to sample faster — sampling and advertising are separate concerns.

nodes.label: BLE Connection Parameter Policy
nodes.rationale: Relaxed 500-1000 ms normally, 100-250 ms during ACTIVE/INTERACTIVE, issued once per transition and never repeatedly. The request is held until the client enables notifications, because a relaxed interval applied while the central is still walking the attribute table stretches every discovery round trip to a full second and a central that times discovery out just drops the link.

nodes.label: Thresholded BLE Notifications
nodes.rationale: Notify only on threshold-crossing change or explicit client request. The last value reported over BLE is stored separately from the previous sensor reading, so a slow drift still notifies once it crosses the delta while an unchanged reading generates no traffic — these are different concepts.

nodes.label: 12-Byte WB_BME280 Characteristic Payload
nodes.rationale: Little-endian: int32 temperature 0.01 degC at offset 0, uint32 pressure Pa at offset 4, uint32 humidity 1/1024 %RH at offset 8. CubeMX generates SizeBme_C = 1, so it is widened to BLE_ENV_PAYLOAD_LEN from the SVCCTL_InitService1 user section in custom_stm.c before aci_gatt_add_char() reads it; the characteristic is already CHAR_VALUE_LEN_VARIABLE.

nodes.label: BLE Connection Must Survive MCU Sleep
nodes.rationale: Entering STOP2 must never disconnect BLE; any change that prevents low-power mode because of BLE is a power regression and must be documented.
nodes.norm_label: ble connection must survive mcu sleep

nodes.label: STOP2 Low-Power Requirement
nodes.rationale: Before entering STOP2 verify no I2C transaction is active, no sensor conversion needs CPU servicing, no OLED transaction is active, the BLE stack permits sleep, and the wake sources (RTC, BLE event, button) are configured.

nodes.label: HSE Clock Restore on STOP2 Exit
nodes.rationale: The real blocker for STOP2. EnterLowPower() switches the core to HSI and drops flash to zero wait states, and CubeMX leaves the restore to the application — both ExitLowPower_1 and _2 user blocks were empty. This app runs HSE at 32 MHz with FLASH_LATENCY_1 and SMPS on HSE, so without a restore the system stayed on HSI 16 MHz from the first wake: every peripheral clock, HAL timeout and the SysTick period silently doubled. ExitLowPower_1 now re-enables HSE, raises flash latency BEFORE the frequency, switches SYSCLK back and puts SMPS back on HSE; ExitLowPower_2 is the case where CPU2 kept HSE running and nothing needs restoring.
nodes.norm_label: hse clock restore on stop2 exit

nodes.label: CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED Trade-Off
nodes.rationale: Left at 1 deliberately: it keeps the debug domain clocked in STOP2 and inflates measured current by roughly a milliamp, so it must be 0 for current measurement and back to 1 to attach a probe. The #else branch of APPD_Init() puts JTAG-only pins in analog mode, so GPIO_PIN_15 was removed from that list because PA15 is the user button; PA13/PA14 and PB3/PB4 still go analog.

nodes.label: Avoid Busy Waiting
nodes.rationale: Busy loops keep the core awake and defeat STOP2; use the SENSOR_IDLE -> TRIGGERED -> READY -> READ state progression instead.

nodes.label: Tick Wraparound and RTC Timing
nodes.rationale: Use unsigned subtraction so 32-bit tick comparisons survive wraparound, and prefer RTC/low-power timers for long intervals since SysTick does not keep running in STOP2.

nodes.label: Explicit Driver Error Handling
nodes.rationale: I2C NACK, missing BME280, invalid chip ID, OLED failure and BLE failure must never be silently ignored; transient sensor errors are recorded and retried on the next scheduled cycle, with a slower retry schedule after repeated failures.

nodes.label: Build-Time Logging Control
nodes.rationale: UART logging significantly affects power measurements, so production/battery tests must be possible with it entirely disabled, and the MCU must never wake solely for debug output.

nodes.label: Power Measurement Instrumentation GPIOs
nodes.rationale: POWER_TRACE_HIGH/LOW around measurements lets a scope, logic analyzer, PPK or Joulescope correlate current with activity; must compile out in production builds.

nodes.label: Phase 3 - Adaptive Sampling
nodes.rationale: Complete in Core/Src/app_env.c. Sampling is no longer polled: an RTC-backed timer-server timer sets CFG_TASK_ENV_MEASURE_ID and a second timer covers the forced-conversion delay setting CFG_TASK_ENV_READ_ID. Stability counts consecutive unchanged 1 Hz samples (ACTIVE_STABLE_SAMPLE_COUNT) rather than using a tick stopwatch, so it stays correct across STOP2 and tick wraparound.

nodes.label: Phase 5 - OLED Sleep
nodes.rationale: app_display.c owns the timeout; DISPLAY_APP_PowerOn/PowerOff/IsPowered in display_app.c own the power abstraction. The panel is powered off at the end of APP_DISPLAY_Init() and only relit by APP_ENV_OnUserInteraction(); a frame is recomposed only when a printed digit changes.

nodes.label: Phase 6 - STM32 Low Power
nodes.rationale: main()'s while(1) contains only MX_APPE_Process(), so each pass ends in UTIL_SEQ_Idle() -> UTIL_LPM_EnterLowPower() -> PWR_EnterStopMode(). CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED is 1 and no longer force-cleared because both debug trace flags are 0. All I2C access is blocking HAL_I2C_Mem_Read/Write so no transfer is ever in flight at idle; the BLE stack holds sleep off itself via UTIL_LPM_SetOffMode(CFG_LPM_APP_BLE). Current measurement on hardware is still open; USB/HSI48 and ADC1 are initialized but unused and could be removed from the .ioc if the measurement disappoints.

nodes.label: Phase 7 - BLE Power Optimization
nodes.rationale: Adv_Request() hardcodes CFG_FAST_CONN_ADV_INTERVAL_*, which sit outside any CubeMX user section in app_conf.h, so they are overridden from USER CODE BEGIN PD in app_ble.c to BLE_ADV_INTERVAL_MIN/MAX to survive regeneration. Slave latency BLE_CONN_LATENCY is 0 and is the next lever; BLE_CONN_SUPERVISION_TIMEOUT must stay above (1 + latency) * interval_max * 2.

nodes.label: Phase 8 - OLED Hardware Power Gating
nodes.rationale: Abstraction is in place but the WeAct module wires OLED VCC directly with no load switch. The rail sequencing already exists guarded by #if defined(OLED_PWR_Pin); adding a P-MOSFET plus an OLED_PWR GPIO_Output label in CubeMX makes those blocks live. ssd1315_basic_init() must be re-run after a rail cycle because the controller loses its configuration — deliberately not wired up while the rail is never cut.

nodes.label: Power Optimization Rule
nodes.rationale: Between two implementations, prefer wake -> minimal work -> schedule next event -> sleep over wake -> wait -> poll -> wait -> poll.

nodes.label: Performance Rule
nodes.rationale: Low power must not make the product feel unresponsive: activity rises temporarily on meaningful events and drops aggressively otherwise. This adaptive behavior is the core architectural principle.

nodes.label: CubeMX User Code Section Discipline
nodes.rationale: Only code inside USER CODE BEGIN/END survives regeneration; the .ioc must not be regenerated unless asked and STM32CubeWB must not be auto-upgraded.

nodes.label: Important Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: No FreeRTOS, filesystem, external flash, Wi-Fi, cloud, complex menu UI, continuous sampling, continuous OLED, or high-rate BLE streaming; the first goal is a small, understandable, measurable low-power BLE environmental monitor.
